question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Hektic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hektic" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "hectic", meaning full of frantic activity; very busy and fast-paced. (अत्यधिक व्यस्त)

◦ Example: She had a hectic week at the office.

• Spelling key: HEC + TIC (with a "c", not a "k").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "Gentle" (mild/soft), "Brilliant" (very bright/clever) and "Kinetic" (relating to motion).

NOTE

• Words ending in the /k/ sound are often spelt "-ic" in English: hectic, kinetic, frantic, drastic, elastic. The spelling "-ktic" is not used.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is mentally ill
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Lunatic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "lunatic" is a person who is mentally ill (insane). (पागल / विक्षिप्त व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: In earlier times, asylums were built to house lunatics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mercenary" — a soldier who fights for money for a foreign army.

• Option 2 "Psychiatrist" — a doctor who treats mental illness (not one who is ill).

• Option 4 "Psychologist" — a person who studies the mind and human behaviour.

NOTE

• Do not confuse: a psychiatrist is a medical doctor (MBBS) who can prescribe medicines, while a psychologist studies behaviour and provides counselling/therapy.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The company's new product received affirmative feedback from customers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. positive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Affirmative" means agreeing, approving or saying 'yes'; positive. So "affirmative feedback" is favourable, encouraging feedback. Its closest synonym here is "positive". (सकारात्मक / स्वीकारात्मक)

◦ Example: The audience gave an affirmative/positive response to the proposal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "critical" (finding fault) is nearly the opposite in this context.

• Option 3 "detailed" (thorough) and Option 4 "reflective" (thoughtful) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of affirmative: positive, favourable, approving, assenting. Antonyms: negative, dissenting. In grammar, an "affirmative sentence" is a positive (non-negative) statement.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She told me / her name but / I'm not remembering / it now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. I'm not remembering.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Remember" is a stative (non-continuous) verb — verbs of mental state are not normally used in the continuous (-ing) form. So "I'm not remembering" is wrong; it should be "I don't remember".

◦ Correct: She told me her name but I don't remember it now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "She told me", "her name but" and "it now" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Common stative verbs not used in the continuous form: know, remember, understand, believe, like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, belong, own, seem. We say "I know", not "I am knowing".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

He bought strange vintage car on auction from the customs department.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. strange vintage car.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Car" is a singular countable noun and needs an article. The segment should be "a strange vintage car" (using the indefinite article "a").

◦ Correct: He bought a strange vintage car at auction from the customs department.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• A singular countable noun cannot stand alone without a determiner (a/an/the/this/my, etc.).

• (Note also that idiomatically we say "at auction", but the marked error segment is the missing article.)

NOTE

• Use "a" before a consonant sound (a car, a strange car) and "an" before a vowel sound (an auction, an hour). Singular countable nouns almost always need an article or other determiner.

question:
Select the most appropriate phrase to replace the underlined word.

She is feeling unwell today, so she will not be going to work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. under the weather.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "under the weather" means feeling unwell / slightly ill. It correctly replaces "unwell". (अस्वस्थ / तबीयत ठीक न होना)

◦ Correct: She is feeling under the weather today, so she will not be going to work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "head in the clouds" (day-dreaming, out of touch with reality).

• Option 2 "face like thunder" (looking very angry).

• Option 3 "chase rainbows" (pursue unrealistic goals). None mean "unwell".

NOTE

• Other idioms for being ill: "off colour", "out of sorts", "at death's door" (very seriously ill), "feeling green".

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Just when they reach the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Just before they reached.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause uses the past perfect ("had departed"), so the other action must be in the simple past and must logically come after the departure. "Just before they reached" the airport, the flight had (already) departed — the sequence and tenses now agree.

◦ Correct: Just before they reached the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "have reached" (present perfect) clashes with the past "had departed".

• Options 2 and 3 use the present tense "reach", which does not match the past narrative.

NOTE

• Past perfect (had + V3) shows the earlier of two past actions; the later action takes the simple past. Here the departure (had departed) happened before they reached (simple past).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Sathish remained unwavering in the face of the assaulting gang, standing as resolute as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. steel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The simile "as resolute as steel" (firm and unshakeable like steel) fits the sense of remaining "unwavering". "Steel" is a strong, hard metal used to suggest firmness and determination. (फ़ौलाद की तरह दृढ़)

◦ Correct: ... standing as resolute as steel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "still" (motionless/quiet), Option 3 "stall" (a booth / to delay) and Option 4 "steal" (to take without permission) are homophones/near-homophones that do not fit.

NOTE

• "Steel" is also used as a verb: "to steel oneself" means to prepare mentally for something difficult. Note the homophone "steal" (to rob).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She confided in me on her anxious, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. about her anxiety.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "confided in me" we need the preposition "about" followed by a noun. "Anxious" is an adjective; the correct noun form is "anxiety". So the segment becomes "about her anxiety". (अपनी चिंता के बारे में)

◦ Correct: She confided in me about her anxiety, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the wrong preposition "on".

• Option 2 uses the adjective "anxious" where a noun is needed.

• Option 4 "regarding herself's anxiousness" is grammatically incorrect ("herself's" is not a valid possessive).

NOTE

• Word forms: adjective anxious → noun anxiety / anxiousness → adverb anxiously. "Confide in (a person) about (something)".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

As long as I live, I shall be obliged to my Uncle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. thankless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obliged" (here) means grateful/thankful/indebted to someone for their help. Its antonym is "thankless" — showing no gratitude / ungrateful. (कृतघ्न — आभारी का विलोम)

◦ Example: I am much obliged (grateful) to you for your help.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "grateful", 2 "pleased" and 4 "indebted" are synonyms of obliged, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of obliged: grateful, indebted, beholden, thankful. Antonyms: thankless, ungrateful, unappreciative. "Thankless" can also mean a task that earns no thanks (a thankless job).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

I had never saw/ such a sight/ before I visited Switzerland.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I had never saw.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "had", the past participle (V3) is required. The past participle of "see" is "seen" (see – saw – seen), not "saw" (which is the simple past). So it should be "I had never seen".

◦ Correct: I had never seen such a sight before I visited Switzerland.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "such a sight" and "before I visited Switzerland" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Past perfect = had + past participle (V3): had seen, had gone, had done. Never use the simple past (saw, went, did) after "had".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please bring some milk from ______ refrigerator in the kitchen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• We use the definite article "the" for a specific, identified thing — here, one particular refrigerator ("in the kitchen"). Both speaker and listener know which one is meant. (निश्चित वस्तु के लिए "the")

◦ Correct: Please bring some milk from the refrigerator in the kitchen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "a/an" are indefinite articles used for a non-specific single thing; they do not fit a particular, known refrigerator.

• Omitting the article ("No article required") is wrong because a singular countable noun needs a determiner.

NOTE

• Use "the" when the noun is unique, already mentioned, or made specific by a phrase like "in the kitchen"; use "a/an" when mentioning a singular countable noun for the first time or in a general sense.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Though Amal took continuous medication, he was not able to __________________ his injury.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. heal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Heal" means to make (a wound/injury) healthy again; to cure. It correctly fits "his injury". (घाव भरना / स्वस्थ करना)

◦ Correct: Though Amal took continuous medication, he was not able to heal his injury.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "heel" (the back part of the foot), Option 3 "hail" (frozen rain / to greet) and Option 4 "hill" (a small mountain) are homophones/near-homophones that do not fit.

NOTE

• Homophones: heal (to cure) vs heel (part of foot); hail (ice pellets / to greet) vs hale (healthy, as in "hale and hearty").

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Wine glass is very fragile; you must handle it with care.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Delicate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fragile" means easily broken or damaged; delicate. Its closest synonym is "delicate". (नाज़ुक / आसानी से टूटने वाला)

◦ Example: The fragile/delicate vase shattered when it fell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Resilient" (able to recover quickly / spring back) and Option 2 "Sturdy" (strong, tough) are antonyms.

• Option 4 "Rough" (not smooth) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fragile: delicate, brittle, frail, flimsy. Antonyms: sturdy, robust, tough, durable, resilient.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence.

The salesman informed the customers that if they had any questions, they could drop a line.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. send a brief letter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "drop a line" means to send a short letter, note or message to someone. So it can be substituted by "send a brief letter". (संक्षिप्त पत्र/संदेश भेजना)

◦ Example: Drop me a line when you reach home safely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "complain against him", 3 "call his secretary" and 4 "come back with the items" do not carry the meaning of the idiom.

NOTE

• Related communication idioms: "drop a line" (send a short message), "give someone a ring/buzz" (phone someone), "touch base" (make contact briefly).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Tara has been playing / cricket with her friends / since noon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is grammatically correct. It uses the present perfect continuous ("has been playing") for an action that started in the past and is still continuing, with "since" correctly marking a point of time ("since noon").

◦ Correct: Tara has been playing cricket with her friends since noon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "has been playing" (present perfect continuous) is correct for a singular subject "Tara".

• "since noon" correctly uses "since" with a point of time.

NOTE

• Present perfect continuous = has/have been + verb-ing. Use "since" with a point of time (since noon, since Monday) and "for" with a length of time (for two hours).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

Surprisingly!/ dark chocolates/ are most bitterer/ in taste.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. are most bitterer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Most bitterer" is a double error: it wrongly combines the superlative marker "most" with the comparative "bitterer". The comparative degree of "bitter" is "bitterer" (or "more bitter") and the superlative is "bitterest" (or "most bitter"). Here the correct form should simply be "bitterer" (comparative) or "more bitter".

◦ Correct: Surprisingly, dark chocolates are bitterer (more bitter) in taste.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Never mix "more/most" with the "-er/-est" ending (no "most bitterer", "more better").

NOTE

• Degrees of "bitter": bitter – bitterer / more bitter – bitterest / most bitter. Use the comparative with "than" and the superlative with "the".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

His business was so successful that Mark was able to _________ at the age of 50.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. retire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Retire" means to stop working (usually because of age) after a long career. As the business was very successful, Mark could afford to retire at 50. (सेवानिवृत्त होना)

◦ Correct: His business was so successful that Mark was able to retire at the age of 50.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "admit" (to confess/allow entry), Option 2 "give up" (to quit/surrender) and Option 3 "succeed" (to achieve success) do not fit the idea of stopping work after success.

NOTE

• "Retire" (stop working) vs "retreat" (withdraw). Related nouns: retirement, retiree. "Give up" implies quitting due to failure, which contradicts "so successful".

question:
Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The permisible limit of vehicle speed has been increased in India by the Road Transport Corporation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. permissible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "permissible", meaning allowed / permitted. The word in the sentence ("permisible") is misspelt. (अनुमेय / स्वीकार्य)

◦ Correct: The permissible limit of vehicle speed has been increased in India ...

• Spelling key: PER + MISS + IBLE (double "s", ends in "-ible").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2's "parmissible", Option 3's "parmitted" and Option 4's "permisibble" are all misspelt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Permissible" comes from "permit"; note the double "s" and the "-ible" ending (not "-able").

NOTE

• Related words: permit (verb/noun), permission (noun), permissible (adjective). Common "-ible" words: possible, visible, permissible, sensible, edible.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence.

As the roller coaster reached its highest point, a surge of addrenalline coursed through her veins, making her heart race with excitement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. adrenaline.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "adrenaline" — a hormone (also called epinephrine) released by the adrenal glands that increases heart rate and prepares the body for "fight or flight". (एड्रेनालाईन)

◦ Correct: ... a surge of adrenaline coursed through her veins ...

• Spelling key: AD + REN + A + LINE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "adrennaline" (double "n"), "adrineline" and "adreneline" all have wrong vowels/letters.

NOTE

• Adrenaline (epinephrine) is secreted by the adrenal glands (located above the kidneys). It raises heart rate, blood pressure and blood sugar during stress or excitement.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. conform.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conform to" means to comply with / behave according to rules, standards or another's way of thinking. The writer does not want to persuade you to conform to his way of thinking. (अनुरूप होना / के अनुसार चलना)

◦ Correct: ... to persuade you to conform to the way the writer thinks or feels.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "affirm" (to state firmly) and Option 2 "confirm" (to verify) do not take "to" in this sense.

• Option 4 "control" does not fit the preposition "to" or the meaning.

NOTE

• The verb "conform" is followed by the preposition "to" (conform to rules/norms). Do not confuse: affirm (assert), confirm (verify), conform (comply).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. between.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "between" is used when referring to two people/things. Here it is "a dialogue between two friends". (के बीच)

◦ Correct: It is really a dialogue between two friends talking about their problems.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "behind" (at the back of), Option 2 "unless" (a conjunction meaning 'if not') and Option 4 "before" (in front of / earlier) do not fit "a dialogue ___ two friends".

NOTE

• Use "between" for two (a talk between two friends) and "among" for more than two (shared among the students). A "dialogue" is a conversation between two parties.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. radical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Radical" (adjective) means thorough, complete or fundamental. A "radical transformation" is a deep, far-reaching change — which fits the idea of changing "the way human beings live". (आमूल-चूल / मौलिक)

◦ Correct: ... there must be a radical transformation in the way human beings live ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "radial" (arranged like rays from a centre) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "avoidable" (able to be avoided) contradicts the need for change.

• Option 4 "highly" is an adverb and cannot directly modify the noun "transformation".

NOTE

• "Radical" can mean fundamental/far-reaching (radical change) or, politically, favouring extreme reform. Synonyms: fundamental, sweeping, drastic, thorough.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. most.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With "the" and a long adjective, we form the superlative with "most". "The most important person" means the single most important person, which fits the emphasis on the teacher. (सबसे — उच्चतम अवस्था)

◦ Correct: The teacher is the most important person in the school ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "much" and Option 3 "more" cannot follow "the ... important" here (comparative "more" would need "than").

• Option 2 "not" reverses the intended meaning.

NOTE

• Superlative of long adjectives: "the most important / the most beautiful". Comparative: "more important than". The word "the" signals the superlative degree.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "of" correctly links "regeneration" with "the mind" — "the regeneration of the mind" (the renewal/rebirth of the mind). (का — संबंध सूचक)

◦ Correct: ... these schools must be centres for the regeneration of the mind.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "under", Option 2 "although" (a conjunction) and Option 4 "off" do not fit the phrase "regeneration ___ the mind".

NOTE

• "Regeneration of" (something) is the standard collocation, like "renewal of", "growth of", "development of". "Of" shows a relationship of belonging or connection.

question: The ________ Polo Club is the home of the Ezra Cup event, the world's oldest polo tournament, started in 1880.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Calcutta Polo Club" is the home of the Ezra Cup, the world's oldest polo tournament, first held in 1880. The Calcutta Polo Club (established 1862) is regarded as the oldest polo club in the world. (कलकत्ता पोलो क्लब — एज़रा कप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Polo is believed to have originated in Manipur in India (locally called "Sagol Kangjei"); the modern game was formalised by the British.

• The Calcutta Polo Club was founded by British soldiers Sherer and Stewart.

NOTE

• India's premier polo tournament today is the Indian Polo Association's national championship; the Manipur Polo International celebrates the game's Indian origins.

question: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) envisaged by the Central Government is called _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mission Karmayogi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) is called "Mission Karmayogi". It was launched in September 2020 to transform capacity building of civil servants and make them more creative, proactive and technology-enabled. (मिशन कर्मयोगी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mission Karmayogi aims to shift from a "rules-based" to a "roles-based" human resource management.

• Its online learning platform is called "iGOT Karmayogi" (Integrated Government Online Training).

NOTE

• The programme is guided by the Prime Minister's Human Resource Council at the apex level and is anchored under the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT).

question: In a food chain of Algae-Shrimp-Fish-Bird, if the energy available at the bird is 4 kJ, then the energy available at the shrimp is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 400 kJ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the 10% Law of Energy Transfer (given by Lindeman), only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed on to the next level.

◦ Food chain: Algae → Shrimp → Fish → Bird.

◦ Energy at Bird = 4 kJ. Fish (previous level) = 4 × 10 = 40 kJ. Shrimp (before Fish) = 40 × 10 = 400 kJ.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The remaining 90% of energy is lost at each level as heat, respiration and life processes.

• Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional (it does not cycle back like nutrients).

NOTE

• Trophic levels: Producers → Primary consumers (herbivores) → Secondary consumers → Tertiary consumers. A "pyramid of energy" is always upright.

question: Who is the first Indian Female Dancer to receive the highest Padma award, Padma Vibhushan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sonal Mansingh was the first Indian female dancer to receive the Padma Vibhushan (India's second-highest civilian award). She is a renowned exponent of Bharatanatyam and Odissi. (सोनल मानसिंह — पद्म विभूषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She received the Padma Bhushan in 1992 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2003.

• The four Padma/Bharat Ratna civilian awards in order of precedence: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

NOTE

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, while Bharatanatyam belongs to Tamil Nadu. Sonal Mansingh was also nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, but they are not enforceable by any court. This concept is mentioned in which Article?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 37.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 37 states that the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws, but they are not enforceable by any court. (अनुच्छेद 37)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The DPSP are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution and were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

• Unlike Fundamental Rights (Part III, justiciable), the DPSP are non-justiciable (cannot be enforced in court).

NOTE

• Article 32 — right to constitutional remedies (called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr Ambedkar).

• Article 38 — the State to promote the welfare of the people and reduce inequalities.

• Article 49 — protection of monuments and places of national importance.

question: Which of the following instruments is played by Shreya Bhattacharjee, an eminent musician from Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shreya Bhattacharjee, an eminent musician from Assam, is known for playing the "Tabla", a popular percussion instrument. (तबला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The tabla is a pair of hand drums used widely in Hindustani classical music; its invention is popularly attributed to Amir Khusrau.

• Famous tabla maestros: Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha, Anindo Chatterjee.

NOTE

• Classification of instruments: Tabla/Dholak – percussion (Avanaddh Vadya); Sitar/Veena – string (Tat Vadya); Flute/Shehnai – wind (Sushir Vadya).

question: According to the census of India 2011, which union territory from the following has the highest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, among the Union Territories, Puducherry had the highest sex ratio at 1037 females per 1000 males. (पुदुचेरी — उच्चतम लिंगानुपात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Among states, Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1084); among all UTs, Daman and Diu had the lowest (618).

• Overall national sex ratio (2011) = 943 females per 1000 males.

NOTE

• Sex ratio = number of females per 1000 males. Haryana had the lowest sex ratio among states (879) in 2011.

question: 'Waiting for a Visa' is a 20-page autobiography of _________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Waiting for a Visa" is a short (about 20-page) autobiographical work by Dr B. R. Ambedkar, written around 1935–36, describing his personal experiences of untouchability and caste discrimination. (डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dr B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution and India's first Law Minister.

• His other works include "Annihilation of Caste", "The Problem of the Rupee" and "Who Were the Shudras?".

NOTE

• Ambedkar founded newspapers like Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat, and led the Mahad Satyagraha (1927) for water rights. He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1990.

question: Which of the following Commissions was set up to investigate the incident of Jallianwala Bagh in 1919?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hunter Commission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Hunter Commission" (Disorders Inquiry Committee), headed by Lord William Hunter, was set up in 1919 to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) at Amritsar. (हंटर आयोग — जलियांवाला बाग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The massacre was ordered by General Reginald Dyer, who fired on an unarmed crowd, killing hundreds.

• Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest, and Udham Singh later killed Michael O'Dwyer (1940) in London.

NOTE

• The Sadler Commission (1917) dealt with university education; the Simon Commission (1927) reviewed constitutional reforms and was boycotted with cries of "Simon Go Back".

question: Name the Union territory with the lowest density of population as per Census of India 2011.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, the Union Territory with the lowest population density was the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, at about 46 persons per sq. km. (अंडमान और निकोबार द्वीप समूह — न्यूनतम जनसंख्या घनत्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Delhi had the highest density among UTs (about 11,320 persons/sq km).

• Among states, Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest density (17) and Bihar the highest (1106).

NOTE

• Population density = total population ÷ total land area (persons per sq. km). India's overall density (2011) was 382 persons/sq km.

question: Which of the following is an artificial port in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai port.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chennai Port (formerly Madras Port) is an artificial (man-made) harbour on the east coast of India. As the natural coastline did not offer shelter, breakwaters were built to create the harbour. (चेन्नई बंदरगाह — कृत्रिम पत्तन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chennai Port is one of the oldest artificial ports and a major port on the Coromandel Coast.

• Mumbai Port and Kolkata Port are natural harbours; Kolkata is a riverine port on the Hooghly.

NOTE

• India has 13 major ports. Kandla (Deendayal Port) is a tidal port in Gujarat, and Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) is India's largest container port.

question: In Maikal hills, which of the following minerals is deposited?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bauxite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Maikal Hills (part of the Satpura range, spread over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh) are rich in bauxite deposits. (मैकाल पहाड़ी — बॉक्साइट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bauxite is the chief ore of aluminium; India's major bauxite-producing states include Odisha, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.

• The Amarkantak plateau in the Maikal range is the source of the Narmada and Son rivers.

NOTE

• Bauxite is refined into alumina (Al₂O₃) and then smelted into aluminium. Odisha is India's largest bauxite producer.

question: Which of the following possesses the largest isolated single cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ostrich egg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ostrich egg is considered the largest known single cell (before fertilisation and development, the yolk of the egg is a single cell). (शुतुरमुर्ग का अंडा — सबसे बड़ी एकल कोशिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The longest cell in the human body is the nerve cell (neuron); the human egg (ovum) is the largest cell in the human body.

• The smallest cell is generally the bacterium Mycoplasma (PPLO).

NOTE

• The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life, discovered by Robert Hooke (1665). The cell theory was proposed by Schleiden and Schwann.

question: Find the acceleration (in m/s2) of a body which accelerates from 5 m/s to 10 m/s in 2 seconds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.5 m/sec2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Acceleration (a) = change in velocity ÷ time taken = (v − u) / t.

◦ Here initial velocity u = 5 m/s, final velocity v = 10 m/s, time t = 2 s.

◦ a = (10 − 5) / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 m/s².

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Acceleration is a vector quantity (it has both magnitude and direction); its SI unit is m/s².

• The three equations of motion: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as.

NOTE

• If velocity decreases, the acceleration is negative (called retardation/deceleration). Uniform acceleration means velocity changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals.

question: Who presides over the House in absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker in the Indian political system?
option_1: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chairperson so nominated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the absence of both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker, the House is presided over by a member from the Panel of Chairpersons — i.e., a "Chairperson so nominated" by the Speaker. (सभापति तालिका का सदस्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Under the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha, the Speaker nominates a Panel of Chairpersons (usually up to 10 members) to preside when the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are absent.

• If none of them is present, any member determined by the House acts as presiding officer.

NOTE

• The Speaker (Article 93) is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha. In the Rajya Sabha, the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman; a Panel of Vice-Chairmen presides in his absence.

question: Which of the following dance forms emotes a play through dancing in which the song is customarily in Manipravala language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mohiniyattam" (Mohiniattam), the classical dance of Kerala, enacts a play through dance in which the songs are customarily in the "Manipravala" language — a blend of Sanskrit and Malayalam. (मोहिनीअट्टम — मणिप्रवाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Mohiniyattam" means the "dance of the Mohini" (the enchantress form of Lord Vishnu); it is a graceful, feminine solo dance.

• It was revived and popularised by the poet Vallathol Narayana Menon through the Kerala Kalamandalam.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: The Home Rule League Movement of Bal Gangadhar Tilak had its base across Karnataka and Maharashtra, but excluding which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Home Rule League (founded April 1916 at Belgaum) operated in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar. Thus Bombay was excluded from Tilak's League. (तिलक की होम रूल लीग — बॉम्बे को छोड़कर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The rest of India, including Bombay city, was covered by Annie Besant's Home Rule League (founded September 1916 at Madras).

• The Home Rule Movement demanded self-government (Swaraj) for India within the British Empire.

NOTE

• "Home Rule" was inspired by the Irish Home Rule Movement. Tilak's famous slogan: "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it."

question: Which of the following is the residential place of Buddhist priests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vihara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Vihara" is the residential place (monastery) of Buddhist monks/priests. It provided shelter and space for meditation and study. (विहार — बौद्ध भिक्षुओं का निवास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A "Stupa" is a hemispherical mound built over the relics of the Buddha (e.g., Sanchi Stupa).

• A "Chaitya" is a Buddhist prayer hall/shrine.

• A "Stambha" is a pillar (e.g., the Ashokan pillars).

NOTE

• The state of Bihar derives its name from "Vihara". Famous ancient viharas/universities include Nalanda, Vikramshila and Odantapuri.

question: Which festival commemorates the death of Hussain Ibn Ali?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muharram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Muharram" commemorates the martyrdom (death) of Hussain ibn Ali, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad, who was killed in the Battle of Karbala (680 CE). The 10th day is observed as "Ashura". (मुहर्रम — इमाम हुसैन की शहादत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Muharram is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar; it is a period of mourning, especially for Shia Muslims.

• "Tazia" processions are taken out in remembrance of the tragedy of Karbala.

NOTE

• Other Islamic festivals: Eid-ul-Fitr (end of Ramadan), Eid-ul-Adha (Bakrid) (festival of sacrifice), Milad-un-Nabi (Prophet's birthday) and Shab-e-Barat (night of forgiveness).

question: The Mawsynram receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world. It is located in which hills?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khasi hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mawsynram, which receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world, is located in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya. (मासिनराम — खासी पहाड़ियाँ, मेघालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nearby Cherrapunji (Sohra), also in the Khasi Hills, is another of the wettest places on Earth.

• The heavy rainfall is due to the funnelling of moisture-laden monsoon winds against the steep hills.

NOTE

• Meghalaya ("abode of clouds") has three hill groups: the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia Hills, inhabited mainly by the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia tribes.

question: Which of the following national income aggregates is generally recognised as National Income of a country?
option_1: Net National Product at Market Prices
option_2: Net National Product at Factor Cost
option_3: Gross National Product at Market Prices
option_4: Gross Domestic Product at Factor Cost
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net National Product at Factor Cost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• National Income of a country is generally recognised as the Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNP at FC). It is the total income earned by the factors of production (land, labour, capital, enterprise) owned by a country's residents. (राष्ट्रीय आय — कारक लागत पर निवल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• NNP at FC = NNP at Market Price − Indirect Taxes + Subsidies.

• NNP = GNP − Depreciation; GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad.

NOTE

• Factor Cost = actual cost of factors of production; Market Price = factor cost + indirect taxes − subsidies. National income data in India is compiled by the NSO (formerly CSO).

question: From which state in India did the legendary volleyball player Jimmy George hail?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Indian volleyball player Jimmy George hailed from Kerala. He was one of India's greatest volleyball players and among the first to play professionally in Europe (Italy). (जिमी जॉर्ज — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Jimmy George was named among the world's best ten volleyball players in his time.

• He was honoured with the Arjuna Award (1976); a stadium in Thiruvananthapuram is named after him.

NOTE

• Volleyball is played between two teams of 6 players each; the sport was invented by William G. Morgan (USA, 1895). It is governed globally by the FIVB.

question: Who among the following has been appointed as the new Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) in June 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Janardan Prasad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Janardan Prasad was appointed as the new Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) in June 2023. (जनार्दन प्रसाद — जीएसआई महानिदेशक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Geological Survey of India (GSI) was established in 1851 and is headquartered in Kolkata.

• It works under the Ministry of Mines and is responsible for geological surveys, mineral exploration and natural-hazard studies.

NOTE

• The GSI was originally founded to locate coal deposits for the railways. Its first major project was surveying the Darjeeling coalfields.

question: Pulakeshin II was the famous ruler of which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chalukya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pulakeshin II was the most famous ruler of the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi (Badami). He is renowned for defeating Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada river. (पुलकेशिन द्वितीय — चालुक्य वंश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Aihole inscription, composed by his court poet Ravikirti, records Pulakeshin II's achievements.

• The Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visited his kingdom, and he exchanged embassies with the Persian ruler Khusrau II.

NOTE

• The Chalukyas of Badami were later defeated by the Rashtrakutas. Pulakeshin II's capital was Vatapi (Badami) in present-day Karnataka.

question: For the development of agriculture, a new department, Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi was established by which of the following Sultans of Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq established a separate department for agriculture called "Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi" to promote and improve cultivation, especially of barren lands. (दीवान-ए-अमीर-कोही — मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He is also known for his controversial schemes — the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token (bronze/copper) currency.

• He ruled from 1325 to 1351 CE and was noted for his learning but "ill-starred" experiments.

NOTE

• Diwan means a department/ministry. Other Sultanate departments: Diwan-i-Wizarat (finance), Diwan-i-Arz (military), Diwan-i-Insha (correspondence), Diwan-i-Risalat (religious affairs).
